questions.question: At which domain separation support level are application properties domain-aware as needed?

explanation.correct: At the Standard support level, application properties are domain-aware as needed. This level includes all aspects of Basic level support plus the ability for service providers to create or modify processes per customer, with the instance owner configuring MVP business logic per tenant.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Basic level focuses on data going into proper domains, not property domain-awareness
Enhanced level builds on Standard; property domain-awareness starts at Standard
Properties can be domain-aware starting at the Standard support level

source.excerpt: Standard - Includes all aspects of Basic level support. Application properties are domain-aware as needed.

questions.question: Which features are available in the extended domain separation functionality for Performance Analytics with the Domain Separation Support plugin? (Choose three)

explanation.correct: The extended functionality available in the Performance Analytics — Domain Separation Support plugin includes: (1) Hierarchical multi-domain configurations to group domains and control score collection, (2) Collect aggregate scores by combining scores from multiple domains in a domain configuration, and (3) Dashboard filtering by domain to show scores by domain or domain aggregate.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Automatic data backup is not a PA domain separation feature
Cross-instance domain replication is not a feature of the PA Domain Separation Support plugin

source.excerpt: Hierarchical multi-domain configurations, Collect aggregate scores, Dashboard filtering by domain. The extended functionality is available in the Performance Analytics — Domain Separation Support plugin.

questions.question:
Evaluate the following statements about domain separation in Event Management:

Statement 1: Impact calculation in Event Management is supported with segregation based on how CIs are segregated.

Statement 2: The discovery process automatically segregates CIs by domain in Event Management.

Which statements are TRUE?

explanation.correct: Statement 1 is TRUE: Impact calculation is supported in Event Management domain separation, with segregation based on the manner in which CIs are segregated. Statement 2 is FALSE: The discovery process does NOT segregate CIs by domain - this is explicitly noted as a limitation in the documentation.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statement 2 is false; discovery does NOT segregate CIs by domain. Statement 1 is true about impact calculation.
Statement 2 is false; the discovery process does not automatically segregate CIs by domain
Statement 1 is true; impact calculation IS supported with CI-based segregation

source.excerpt: Impact calculation - Supported. Segregation is based on the manner in which CIs are segregated. Dynamic CI groups - Partially supported. Note: The discovery process does not segregate CIs by domain.

questions.question: Which API enables copying Performance Analytics records between different domains on the same instance?

explanation.correct: The PADomainUtils API enables you to copy Performance Analytics records between different domains on the same instance. This is useful for propagating PA configurations across domains.

wrongAnswers.explanation: GlideDomain is not the specific API for copying PA records between domains
DomainCopy is not a standard ServiceNow API for this purpose
GlideRecord is a general data access API, not specifically designed for PA domain copying

source.excerpt: PADomainUtils - Global: The PADomainUtils API enables you to copy Performance Analytics records between different domains on the same instance.

questions.question: A sample use case for Enhanced domain separation support level states: 'Tenant-customers of a shared environment must be able to modify the impact, urgency, or priority matrix to set priority within their domain.' This demonstrates which capability?

options.text: Tenant self-service configuration of business logic

explanation.correct: This sample use case demonstrates the Enhanced support level capability where tenants of the instance can configure minimum viable product (MVP) business logic and data parameters for themselves. The ability to modify the priority matrix within their domain is tenant self-service configuration.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Basic data separation doesn't allow tenants to modify business logic like priority matrices
This is tenant self-configuration, not service provider creating processes for customers (which is Standard level)
This is not about delegating global admin functions, but about tenants configuring their own domain business logic

source.excerpt: Enhanced - Sample use case: Tenant-customers of a shared environment must be able to modify the impact, urgency, or priority matrix to set priority within their domain.

questions.question: What support level does CMDB have for domain separation?

explanation.correct: CMDB has Standard level domain separation support. This includes all aspects of Basic level support, plus domain-aware application properties and business logic that allows service providers to create or modify processes per customer tenant.

wrongAnswers.explanation: CMDB has Standard, not Basic support
Enterprise is not a standard domain separation support level

source.excerpt: Support level: Standard. Includes all aspects of Basic level support. Application properties are domain-aware as needed. Business logic: The service provider (SP) creates or modifies processes per customer.

questions.question: Which CMDB features support domain separation? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: CMDB Health and CMDB Query Builder both support domain separation. This allows domain-specific health monitoring and querying of configuration items within appropriate domain boundaries.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Global platform settings are instance-wide, not domain-separated
Instance time zone is a global setting

source.excerpt: The following topics provide details about domain separation in Configuration Management (CMDB) modules: Domain separation in CMDB Health, Domain separation and CMDB Query Builder, Domain separation and CMDB Identification and Reconciliation.
